question: Should OpenClaw permanently expose `plugin-sdk/archive`, `plugin-sdk/root-walk`, and `plugin-sdk/secret-file` as supported external plugin APIs?
rationale: These three new export-map entries are compatibility-sensitive plugin SDK contracts, so a maintainer must choose the intended long-term public boundary rather than treating their inclusion as a mechanical refactor detail.

options.title: Approve the focused SDK subpaths
options.body: Keep the three documented subpaths as supported plugin APIs and merge only after the published dependency and frozen-install proof are complete.

options.title: Keep the migration internal
options.body: Remove the public subpaths and adapt bundled callers through internal or existing SDK seams so fs-safe adoption does not expand the external API.

recommendation.title: Approve the focused SDK subpaths
recommendation.body: Keep the three documented subpaths as supported plugin APIs and merge only after the published dependency and frozen-install proof are complete.
